title: Bus-Invert Coding
constraints: Encoder: on a rising edge with `valid`, compare `din` with the **current** bus value. If their Hamming distance is **greater than 4**, drive `bus_q <= ~din` and `inv <= 1`, otherwise `bus_q <= din` and `inv <= 0`. Without `valid` the bus holds (no toggles).
Decoder (combinational): `dout = inv ? ~bus_q : bus_q`, which always recovers the last transmitted word.
`toggles` accumulates the number of bus wires that changed on each update, **including** the `inv` wire (16-bit). This is the switching activity the coding minimizes.
hints: Hamming distance = popcount(din ^ bus_q). A popcount of 8 bits fits in a small adder tree.
Coding bounds the data-wire toggles per transfer at 4 (instead of 8). Count the `inv` wire when it toggles too.

examples.check: inverts when more than half the bits flip
